2_Introduction: The PSCs demonstrated improved PCE of 25.3045% (with FF of 82.5803%, VOC of 1.1605 V, and JSC of 26.403 mA/cm²). 1.65 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0 perovskite precursors were prepared. The layer was cast via a two-step spin approach: initially at 1000 rpm for 5 s, then accelerated to 5500 rpm for 30 s. 150 µL of CB as antisolvent was dripped onto the substrate quickly at the last 15 s during the second spinning step. It was then heated at 110 °C for 15 min, resulting in the formation of the perovskite thin films.
3_Result_Discussion: The optimized perovskite crystallization, employing a 1.65 mol/L triple-cation Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₅FA₀.₉PbI₃ precursor, was governed by a precisely timed antisolvent drip during the high-speed spin-coating stage, which rapidly induced supersaturation to promote a high nucleation density and direct the formation of a pinhole-free, compact morphology. The inclusion of small-radius Cs⁺ cations at the A-site enhanced phase stability by optimizing the Goldschmidt tolerance factor and suppressing undesirable hexagonal polytypes, while the subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C facilitated complete solvent removal and grain growth, thereby minimizing residual PbI₂ phases and reducing grain boundary defect density. This controlled crystallization process yielded a high-quality film with enhanced structural uniformity, which directly mitigated non-radiative recombination losses and improved charge carrier transport, ultimately leading to a champion power conversion efficiency of 25.3045% with a VOC of 1.1605 V, a JSC of 26.403 mA/cm², and an FF of 82.5803%.
